item.title: No Tools for This
item.description:
Stagnant

I feel stagnant. My entire life has always been in pursuit of something: challenging myself in various technical or creative fields, albeit never mastering any. I have worked with physical tools since childhood, later studying architecture, working in graphic design, collaborating on electronic projects with a friend, then moving to America, relearning architecture with a focus on sustainability, then photography, electronic music, and programming again, first creating free tools for others and later working on one of the most popular software packages in the world. I haven’t quite figured out what the driver has been, but I like to think it is curiosity, and not the desire to be worthy of others’ attention or love.

item.title: Eulogy
item.description:
I knew Ehsan for all of 45 McYears. He was a man who stood taller than those around him with his decency and kindness. If, as Sir Isaac Newton suggested, we stand on the shoulders of giants, were we to stand on his mans shoulders, we could see the stars he is now a part of without a space ship.

C. Sykes

item.title: Blast Off
item.description: I am not liked, and not very popular among most human beings. I wish I could take my backpack and books and blast off to another planet; Keeping to search, to love, to laugh, to learn, to explore, etc.

item.title: PS,LP,LB,FA
item.description:
You feel pain. It is not physical. Physical pain is easy. It is external. You cut the cords; it frees you from the pain and lets you focus on the fix. Psychological pain is different. It is internal. There are no cords to cut.

The pain is from a fire inside you. When it is consistently fed stuff to burn, it is ok. But when it runs out of fuel, it starts burning You.

item.title: Debug Me
item.description:
I wish I could see myself from outside of this body; as a third observer. A lot of times I think I’m right. But the reactions I get, tell a different story. I care so much about things that aren’t that important to others. I think the survival formula that I follow has different constants applied, compared to the norm. Most probably it has a deep psychological reason.

Maybe it would be better if I could attach a debugger to myself. Maybe even a serial TTY would be enough so I can see the log messages spitted out from my brain. I would spend the rest of my days figuring out why I think or react the way I do.
